name: DUNCAN, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the state's failure to appoint counsel for an extended period violates the right to counsel and dismissal without prejudice is the appropriate remedy after specific timeframes.

name: Flynn, C. J.
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: Flynn, C.J.
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: James, J.
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: GARRETT, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the ballot title's caption, "yes" result statement, and summary needed modification to accurately reflect the measure's major effects, including the elimination of school district discretion and the non-speculative fiscal consequences of funding following the student.

name: Ortega, P. J.
description: Concurred, argued that all of Ballot Measure 114 is facially valid under Article I, section 27, as it constitutes a reasonable regulation to promote public safety without unduly frustrating the right to armed self-defense.

name: GARRETT, J.
description: Concurred, authored the main opinion, finding that the defendant's mental health attributes did not provide a societal standard to reduce culpability for the crime committed with the requisite mental state, thus the mandatory minimum sentence was not disproportionate.

name: Balmer, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the majority's holding was more limited than the broad rule the defendant had proposed regarding personal characteristics in proportionality analysis.

name: Bushong, J.
description: Other, did not participate in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: Duncan, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Court of Appeals erred in rejecting the defendant's appellate argument on preservation grounds, and remanded the case for further proceedings on the merits of the double jeopardy claim.

name: Bushong, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the majority opinion's detailed discussion of the merits of the double jeopardy claim and related legal principles was unnecessary dicta and should not influence the Court of Appeals on remand.

name: Baldwin, Senior Judge
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: JAMES, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the lack of a "right" to employment does not, as a matter of law, prevent a plaintiff from proving economic damages for lost future wages, and that this is an issue of proof and causation, not pleading.

name: BUSHONG, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the record did not demonstrate that the trial court's decision to deny the defendant's constitutional right to retained counsel of choice was a permissible exercise of its discretion, thus requiring reversal and remand for a new trial.

name: GARRETT, J.
description: Concurred, argued that Governor Kotek lacked authority to revoke the conditional commutation because plaintiff had already completed her sentence, and the terms of the commutation and acceptance agreement did not grant such authority after sentence expiration.

name: Walters, Senior Judge, Justice pro tempore
Masih, J.
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: JAMES, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Court of Appeals erred by analyzing the backpack seizure under a criminal framework instead of an administrative one, and that the seizure of the backpack was a significant interference with possessory interests.

name: DUNCAN, J.
description: Concurred, arguing that the totality of circumstances, including the defendant's probation status and the coercive environment, made the interrogation compelling, requiring Miranda warnings.

name: BALMER, S. J.
description: Concurred, arguing that the state's conduct, including offering benefits and implicitly guiding Layman's investigation after the second proffer meeting, objectively conveyed that Layman was authorized to act as a state agent, thus violating the defendant's right to counsel.

name: Nelson, J.
description: Did not participate in the decision of this case.

name: James, J.
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: GARRETT, J.
description: Concurred, delivered the majority opinion that the UTPA provisions do not require a materiality element and are constitutional, reversing the Court of Appeals' decision.

name: DUNCAN, J.
description: Concurred, argued that detectives violated the defendant's right to counsel under Article I, section 11, of the Oregon Constitution by questioning him about charged FIP crimes without notifying his counsel, requiring suppression of the resulting evidence.

name: NELSON, J.
description: Concurred, argued that ORS 138.105(5) precludes appellate review of legal challenges to a conviction based on a guilty or no contest plea, interpreting "conviction" as the judicial determination of guilt reflected in the judgment.

name: Nakamoto, J.
description: Other, did not participate in the decision of this case.

name: NELSON, J.
description: Concurred, argued that while the Court of Appeals erred in its reasoning regarding the materiality of the lost video and the defendant's guilty plea attempt, the defendant ultimately failed to establish a causal connection between the unexplained delay and the prejudice from the lost video, as the video would likely have been overwritten regardless of the delay.

name: BALMER, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the five-day warrantless retention of the defendant's phone was unlawful, but the error in admitting derivative evidence was harmless, thus affirming the conviction.

name: Baldwin, Senior Judge, Justice pro tempore
DeHoog, J.
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: GARRETT, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Oregon Constitution grants a defendant the right to have counsel present for consultation during grand jury testimony, as it is a critical stage of prosecution.

name: Landau, Senior Judge, Justice pro tempore
Nakamoto, Senior Judge, Justice pro tempore
BALMER, J.
description: Concurred, argued that voters with inactive registrations are not "qualified voters" under Article IV, section 1, because they are not presently eligible to vote, and therefore their signatures on initiative petitions cannot be counted.

name: DUNCAN, J.
description: Concurred, authored the majority opinion, which overruled the Brown per se exigency rule and affirmed the suppression of evidence because the state failed to prove actual exigent circumstances.

name: Landau, Senior Judge, Justice pro tempore
Balmer, J.
description: Did not participate in the consideration or decision of this case.

name: KISTLER, S.J.
description: Concurred, argued that a defective waiver of a preliminary hearing does not deprive a circuit court of subject matter jurisdiction, reversing the Court of Appeals decision.

name: WALTERS, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that the court has authority to modify constitutional deadlines to ensure reapportionment occurs based on federal census data and in time for the election cycle, given the unforeseen delay in census data release.

name: WALTERS, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that the trial court's order compelling the defendant to unlock her cell phone violated Article I, section 12, of the Oregon Constitution because the state failed to prove beyond a reasonable doubt that it already knew the information the act would communicate, and the order did not prohibit the state from using the compelled act against the defendant.
